processing: Made as steamed green tea in the usual sencha way.
harvest_season: Spring, slightly early, about two days before Yabukita and at the same time as Sayamakaori.
appearance_dry: Green needles with a leaf colour close to Yabukita, as is usual for sencha.
appearance_liquor: Clear yellow-green, typical of steamed Japanese green tea.
appearance_wet: Soft mid-green leaf, as is usual for sencha.
taste_profile: A clean, tidy taste and aroma, with quality rated on a par with Yabukita.

brewing.notes: Straightforward sencha settings. It makes a fair test of a clean, modern Saitama green tea.

vintage_note: As with other Japanese green teas, it is sold as the current year's spring harvest and best drunk within a year. As a newer regional cultivar, it is mostly found through Saitama makers, and early first-flush lots are the ones to look for.
description:
Sainomidori is a modern Saitama cultivar and a seedling of Sayamakaori. It keeps Sayamakaori's early timing, with quality rated close to Yabukita.

It is handled as ordinary sencha. Its leaf colour sits near Yabukita's, and the taste and aroma are described as clean and refreshing.

Brew it the sencha way. Little has been published on how it changes from steep to steep, so taste as you go and keep later steeps short.

For a grower the attraction is strong resistance to anthracnose, reducing the need for spraying, along with better resistance to white peach scale than Yabukita and first-flush yield above Yabukita's.

Try it next to Sayamakaori, its parent, for a direct view of what breeding changed.
history: Saitama breeders selected Sainomidori from a naturally pollinated Sayamakaori seedling. Prefectural documents differ on the date: one gives registration on 5 September 2003 as Norin 50, another gives 2006, and a table of adopted cultivars shows 2004.
